summary: accounts-timeline@12.3.7 fetches and executes an obfuscated binary dropper on install and require
details: The package's postinstall hook ("node setup.js || true") and its main entry index.js (which side-effect requires./setup inside a try/catch) both trigger a binary-dropper routine. setup.js reconstructs a set of Cloudflare Workers hostnames from split string fragments (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev and siblings 100-416, 101-adf, 102-baf, 103-070) and downloads a platform-specific executable via https.get, with a DNS-TXT covert-channel fallback that reassembles a base64 payload across numbered subdomains of well1.site (tin/tina/ldr/win.dl.well1.site). The fetched bytes are written to /var/tmp or %TEMP% under a masquerading name (dotnet_diag_<tag>.exe or.cache_<tag>), chmodded 0755 on POSIX, and launched via execFile with {detached:true, windowsHide:true}. The download is unpinned and unhashed, the destinations are anonymous *.workers.dev hosts assembled at runtime to evade static inspection, and the require()-time trigger means the chain fires even in --ignore-scripts environments as soon as any dependent imports the package.
